title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The group 𝔊^+ is the profinite SL(2,Z)^. It contains the torsion generators ρ (order 6, with ρ^3 = −1) and σ (order 4, with σ^2 = −1), so the centre is μ = {1, ρ^3} = {1, σ^2} = {±1}. The larger group 𝔊 also contains elements τ of 'determinant −1', which anticommute with σ (στ = −τσ, as on the previous page). 𝔊^q is a normal subgroup of 𝔊^+ (the notation varies across the neighbouring pages as 𝔊^q / 𝔊^ς). Z_{ρ,σ} is defined on pp. 577–578. It is a group of automorphism-type data u, read here as automorphisms of 𝔊^+ together with signs ε_2, ε_3, subject to conditions a)–d) of (4):
- a) u(ρ) is conjugate to ρ^{ε_3};
- b) u(σ) is conjugate to σ^{ε_2}, both modulo 𝔊^q;
- d) a condition tied to the quotient 𝔊^+/𝔊^q.
The previous page completes the proof that the defining conditions are multiplicative. It constructs the product α'' = ε'_2 ε'_3 u'(ατ')(α'τ') with the correct sign character.

This page.
(1) A crossed-out remark. For b) to be multiplicative one only needs u to normalise the image of L_0 in 𝔊^+/𝔊^q, i.e. u(σ) ≡ ±σ mod 𝔊^q, rather than all of a).
(2) If 𝔊 is 'large enough', the projection Z_{ρ,σ} → Aut(𝔊^+) is injective (12), cf. p. 578. So Z_{ρ,σ} is realised as a group of automorphisms of profinite SL_2.
(3) Three examples in the universal case.
- a) 𝔊^q = 𝔊^+ = SL(2,Z)^. Condition d) is empty. a) and b) just say u(ρ) ~ ρ^{ε_3} and u(σ) ~ σ^{ε_2}, recovering definition (6) of p. 577. Hence (13): Z_{ρ,σ} = M(0)·L_0^𝔊 = M^𝔊[0] = M[0]. Here M(0) is the genus-0 GT-type 'multiplier' group and L_0 an inner/Lego part.
- b) 𝔊^q = Π = Π_0 × μ, i.e. Γ(2)^ ≅ F_2^ × {±1}, with Π_0 ≅ π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}). One finds (14): Z_{ρ,σ} = M(0)·L_0^Π = M^Π[0] = M^![0], to be compared with Z^!_{ρ,σ} of part V n°8. The left margin notes that a priori Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ M_{0,3}-type groups. It also notes that in case b) Z_{ρ,σ} visibly acts trivially on 𝔊^+/𝔊^q.
- c) 𝔊^q = Π_0. Conditions a) and b) are unchanged because μ is central. The next page shows d) becomes stricter: Z ∩ 𝔊^+ = L_0^{Π_0}, of index 2. The result is Z = M''(0)·L_0^{Π_0}, the kernel of the character ε_2.

Purpose. Grothendieck is testing whether the genus-0/1 Teichmüller–GT-type groups M[0], M^![0] can be characterised intrinsically. The characterisation is as stabilisers in Aut(SL_2^) of the torsion conjugacy classes, relative to a chosen normal subgroup 𝔊^q. He also tracks how the answer depends on 𝔊^q. On the next page he proposes redefining Z using a complement 𝔊^q_0 with 𝔊^q = 𝔊^q_0 × μ, so that the answer stays M^![0].
errors: The first remark is struck through. Grothendieck apparently judged the weakened sufficient condition (u(σ) ≡ ±σ mod 𝔊^q) wrong or irrelevant.
The injectivity claim (12) is stated only under the vague hypothesis '𝔊 assez gros' and refers back to p. 578; it is not proved here.

In case c) the equality Z = M[0]-type is not stated here. The next page shows that the naive definition gives an index-2 smaller group, so the definition of Z_{ρ,σ} is not yet stable under changing 𝔊^q. Grothendieck flags this and modifies it.

ideas.what: Realising a GT-type group (M[0], M^![0]) as a group of automorphisms of profinite SL(2,Z) that send the torsion elements ρ, σ to conjugates of powers of themselves, with injectivity into Aut(SL_2^)
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT^ on SL_2(Z)^ / genus-one mapping class groups; GT^ as an automorphism group of profinite (braid/mapping-class) groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps (1997), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Nakamura; later Minamide–Nakamura (Out of profinite braid groups), Horel and Boavida–Horel–Robertson (GT^ as automorphisms of profinite operads)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme describes GT acting on the Teichmüller tower; this explicit stabiliser description inside Aut(SL_2^) is not, to my knowledge, published.

ideas.what: Dependence of the stabiliser group on the chosen normal subgroup 𝔊^q (SL_2^, Γ(2)^ ≅ F_2^ × μ, F_2^), giving M[0], M^![0], and an index-2 subgroup M''[0]_0 respectively
ideas.modern_name: Relative/congruence versions of GT-type groups; kernels of the sign character ε_2

ideas.what: Multiplicativity of the sign-twisted conditions, using τ with τσ = −στ
ideas.modern_name: group-law verification in an extension of GL_2 type

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes characterising GT-type groups (M[0], M^![0]) intrinsically as the groups Z_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms of profinite SL(2,Z), or of an extension by τ. These preserve the conjugacy classes of the torsion elements ρ, σ up to signs and are compatible with a normal subgroup 𝔊^q. He finds the answer depends on 𝔊^q and tries to repair this with a central complement 𝔊^q_0. A clean general theorem identifying such stabilisers with GT^-type groups for arbitrary 𝔊^q is not carried through.
missed.quote: Si 𝔊 est "assez gros", l'homomorphisme de projection est injectif (12) Z_{ρ,σ} ↪ Aut(𝔊^+) ... (13) Z_{ρ,σ} = M(0).L_0^𝔊 = M^𝔊[0] = M[0]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This parallels recent work describing GT^ as an automorphism group (Minamide–Nakamura on Out of profinite braid groups; Horel on profinite operads). It suggests a genus-one / SL_2^ variant with torsion-conjugacy conditions, of which I know no explicit published counterpart.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a substantive but sketchy intrinsic characterisation of GT-type groups as automorphism groups of profinite SL_2 preserving torsion classes, with a case analysis over normal subgroups. The idea of GT acting on profinite SL_2 / genus-one groups is known in the literature. The specific stabiliser formulation and its dependence on 𝔊^q is an unpublished detail, but not shocking.
transcription_corrections: The notation alternates between 𝔊^q and 𝔊^ς (the next page uses ς) for the same normal subgroup.
In example b) the image reads 'M(0).L_0^Π = M^Π[0] = M^![0]', consistent with the transcription; the margin adds 'M^![0] = M^Π[0]'.
'redonnent [?] sur la définition (6) p. 577' is likely 'reviennent à la définition (6) p. 577'.
The left marginal note begins 'NB A priori (ou explicit.)'. It compares Z_{ρ,σ} with M_{0,3}-type groups, and its reading is uncertain.
